articles.title: API search or vector search for an agent
articles.question: MCP/API search or vector search — which should an agent call?
articles.summary: One question through 4 XERJ MCP tools returned 3 different result sets. Hybrid RRF returned 6 documents and merged both lists on the default lexical embedder.

articles.title: Can ChatGPT search a folder on my laptop?
articles.question: Can ChatGPT search a folder on my laptop, or do I need something else?
articles.summary: xerj mcp is a stdio MCP server that proxies 10 tools to a running XERJ node, so an agent reads an indexed local folder instead of opening files itself.

articles.title: Make an agent cite a file instead of dumping it
articles.question: I need my agent to find a passage and cite the file, not dump the whole tree. How?
articles.summary: Index the repository with xerj autoindex, then call xerj_search through xerj mcp. One captured call returned the file and line for 2 symbols without opening a file.

articles.title: Should agent memory use a graph?
articles.question: Ask HN: Anyone using knowledge graphs for LLM agent memory/context management?
articles.summary: XERJ builds a bounded link index over indexed documents, not a graph database. Our capture found 7 edges, answered 1 and 2 hops, and refused 3.

articles.title: Stop agent memory filling with duplicate notes
articles.question: How do I dedup agent memory?
articles.summary: Send dedup true on the store call and XERJ returns the existing id instead of a second document. The write path runs no model and made no outbound call.

articles.title: Evidence behind agent-memory links
articles.question: Agent memory: knowledge graphs aren't enough, we need a know-how graph
articles.summary: Every detected link in XERJ carries the exact line that taught it. All 7 edges in our capture had an evidence quote, and unlink wrote a tombstone.

articles.title: Give two agents private memory on one laptop
articles.question: How do I keep one agent's memory from leaking into another agent's?
articles.summary: XERJ keeps agent memory on local disk and made 0 outbound connections in our capture. Roles are stored but not enforced, so scoped API keys do the work.

articles.title: Store user preferences an agent can recall later
articles.question: How do people store user preferences so an agent can recall them next week?
articles.summary: XERJ keeps agent memory in a reserved index inside the data directory. We stored two memories, restarted the node, recalled both, then forgot one by id.

articles.title: Set the MCP memory storage path
articles.question: Memory MCP ignores custom storage path setting
articles.summary: XERJ has no separate memory path. Agent memory lives in the node data directory as .xerj-memory-{namespace}, and the MCP server stores nothing itself.

articles.title: Agent memory on a laptop, no extra database
articles.question: I want persistent agent memory without standing up Postgres or Qdrant. What do people use?
articles.summary: Our capture ran agent memory on one XERJ process with three loopback sockets, no second data service, and a peak resident size of 100,928 kB.

articles.title: Audit a PHP codebase with an index, not grep
articles.question: How do I search a large PHP repo for dangerous sinks without reading every file?
articles.summary: The published WordPress core audit indexed the tree as queryable facts, then read only the survivors. Core came back hardened, and that negative is the result.

articles.title: Index a reference library for a coding agent
articles.question: How do I set up reference coding so the agent retrieves a mechanism before writing code?
articles.summary: Clone the library you are about to write against, index it with xerj autoindex, and retrieve the passage first. The published study, with the tracks where it loses.

articles.title: How do I reduce embedding API cost?
articles.question: My embedding bill is too high
articles.summary: XERJ embeds documents inside the node by default, so a captured lexical run made 0 outbound calls. Proxy mode sent exactly 2 calls for the same 100 documents.

articles.title: Local search offline with no cloud embeddings
articles.question: I want local search that works offline, no cloud embeddings. What are my options?
articles.summary: XERJ embeds locally in two ways. The default lexical embedder needs no model at all, and --embed-mode neural loads a cached MiniLM model on the CPU.

articles.title: When are neural embeddings worth turning on?
articles.question: Do I even need embeddings for search, or is full-text enough?
articles.summary: Embeddings only helped when we opted into the neural embedder. On XERJ's lexical default, kNN promoted coffee storage above the synonyms for the query car.

articles.title: Can I full-text search my browser history file?
articles.question: Is there a way to full-text search my browser history?
articles.summary: Copy the Chrome History SQLite file and index it. A captured run made titles and URLs queryable, left the source unchanged, and missed 40 WAL rows.

articles.title: Find every place a config key is set in a repo
articles.question: How do I find every place a config key is set across YAML and XML in a repo?
articles.summary: XERJ autoindex indexes YAML and XML config files as full-text documents, maps 9 fields including body and title, and answers one bool query across both.

articles.title: How do I find out what is in a messy data folder?
articles.question: I dropped a messy data folder on an agent. How should it figure out what's inside before searching?
articles.summary: Point xerj autoindex at the folder, then read xerj autoindex map: every dataset it inferred, the fields and types, the time range, and every file it refused.

articles.title: How do I full-text search a SQLite database?
articles.question: How do I full-text search a SQLite database?
articles.summary: xerj autoindex reads a SQLite file read-only and turns each table into an index. A captured WAL-mode run indexed 400 of 450 committed rows and changed no bytes.

articles.title: How do I index a CSV with many columns?
articles.question: How to index CSV files with big number of columns/fields
articles.summary: xerj autoindex infers a mapping for a wide CSV with no schema work. A captured 120-column file produced 128 mapped fields and an exact terms aggregation.

articles.title: How do I index Markdown into Elasticsearch?
articles.question: What is the best way to index Markdown documents into Elasticsearch?
articles.summary: XERJ autoindex indexes Markdown as the txt-prose family and answers the Elasticsearch API, but it maps no headings array and keeps the hash in the title.

articles.title: How do I run syntax-aware code search?
articles.question: Is there a syntax-aware code search tool for refactoring?
articles.summary: XERJ indexes source files with a defs field and a symbols array, so one query finds declarations with kind, name and line while another finds raw text.

articles.title: How do I search a Confluence export?
articles.question: How do I search my Confluence export?
articles.summary: Point xerj autoindex at an unzipped Confluence HTML space export. A captured run kept page titles, nested page bodies, and the attachment tree.

articles.title: How do I search a folder of CSV exports?
articles.question: I have a directory of CSV exports. How do I query them without opening each one in Excel?
articles.summary: Point xerj autoindex at the folder once. A captured run split 3 CSV files across 2 schemas into 2 indices and answered one query across both of them.

articles.title: How do I search a folder of mixed documents?
articles.question: I have a folder of PDFs, Word docs, and markdown. How do I search all of them at once?
articles.summary: Index a folder of PDFs, Word docs and markdown with one xerj autoindex command, then search the contents. A captured 6-file run indexed 51 documents into 2 indices.

articles.title: How do I search a folder of PDF papers?
articles.question: I downloaded a bunch of papers as PDFs. How do I search across them?
articles.summary: One xerj autoindex command indexes the folder, then a match_phrase query reads every PDF. A captured run hit all 3 born-digital files and refused a scanned one.

articles.title: How do I search a folder of Word contracts?
articles.question: How do I search through a folder of contracts in .docx?
articles.summary: Index a folder of DOCX contracts with one xerj autoindex command and search their paragraphs. A captured run also shows the decompression guard refusing a file.

articles.title: How do I search a Slack JSON export?
articles.question: How do I search a Slack or Discord JSON export?
articles.summary: Point xerj autoindex at an unzipped Slack export. A captured run found a threaded reply, kept ts, thread_ts and user, and round-tripped Japanese text.

articles.title: How do I search Kubernetes pod logs?
articles.question: Grep for specific text from kubernetes multiple pods
articles.summary: Collect the pod logs to disk first, then index the folder. A captured run answered 1 phrase query across 3 pods and returned 18 hits, 6 per pod.

articles.title: How do I stop my agent reading the whole repo?
articles.question: How do I stop my agent from reading the whole repo into context?
articles.summary: Index the tree once with xerj autoindex, then let the agent query the defs and symbols fields instead of opening files. A dry run first prints every ignore rule.

articles.title: Is it efficient to index PDF files?
articles.question: Is it inefficient to index PDF files into a search engine?
articles.summary: PDF extraction is the slowest family XERJ parses. XERJ runs it in an isolated worker sized from free memory, caps it 5 ways, and refuses image-only files.

articles.title: Let an agent look up endpoints in an API spec
articles.question: My agent needs to look up endpoints in a big OpenAPI spec. What's the right way?
articles.summary: Index the spec file itself. A captured run found route names, operation descriptions and operationIds in both the JSON and the YAML serialization.

articles.title: Search .ipynb notebooks and the .py files beside them
articles.question: I need to find a function I wrote in a notebook months ago. How do I search all .ipynb files?
articles.summary: A captured run indexed one document per notebook cell, with cell_type, execution_count and the nbformat cell id, so a hit names the exact cell.

articles.title: Search a .csv.gz or .json.gz without unzipping it
articles.question: How do I search gzipped CSV exports?
articles.summary: Gzip is a wrapper, not a family. autoindex unwraps it and sniffs the inner CSV or JSON, so a compressed export becomes typed fields rather than one opaque blob.

articles.title: Search a help-center you saved as HTML
articles.question: I saved a bunch of docs pages as HTML. How do I search that?
articles.summary: XERJ autoindex indexes a static HTML export from local disk, extracts title and a headings array per page, and fetched 0 non-loopback peers in our capture.

articles.title: Search a JSON export of support tickets
articles.question: I have a JSON export of support tickets. How do I search it like a real help-center search?
articles.summary: Index the exported ticket JSON on disk. A captured run returned 36 description hits with per-ticket locators and an exact status count of 30 per status.

articles.title: Search a SQL dump without restoring it
articles.question: I have a 2GB SQL dump. How do I find rows mentioning a customer without loading it into Postgres?
articles.summary: xerj autoindex parses a MySQL-style .sql file directly, with no database server, and makes every INSERT value searchable. A captured run indexed 321 documents.

articles.title: Search BVH motion-capture files
articles.question: How do I search motion-capture data?
articles.summary: xerj autoindex detects the bvh family and extracts frames, frame_time_s, duration_s, joint_count and a joints keyword array. The family produces no body field.

articles.title: Search gzipped logs without decompressing them
articles.question: How do I search gzipped logs without decompressing the whole file?
articles.summary: XERJ autoindex decompresses a .gz log once at index time. In our capture the plain and gzip copies returned identical counts, identical hits and one date field.

articles.title: Search JSON logs and gzip logs in one folder
articles.question: What's the easiest way to search JSON logs plus some old gzip text logs in the same folder?
articles.summary: xerj autoindex detects JSON arrays, JSONL logs and gzipped logs in one folder, infers the date field and answers exact filters. One run returned 386 ERROR hits.

articles.title: Search markdown notes and PDFs in one vault
articles.question: What's the best way to search markdown notes and PDFs in the same vault?
articles.summary: A captured XERJ run indexed a vault of markdown notes and returned text from inside a PDF attachment and a DOCX attachment, plus wikilink edges between the notes.

articles.title: Search Unity scenes and the C# beside them
articles.question: How do I search a Unity project's assets?
articles.summary: xerj autoindex detects the unity and unity-meta families, splits a scene into one index per Unity class, and joins an asset to its .meta record by path.

articles.title: Why does my Notion export duplicate titles?
articles.question: API sync/export duplicates Notion titles in pages, databases, search results
articles.summary: A captured run indexed a Notion Markdown export twice and got the same 8 documents with byte-identical ids. The duplicates come from the export layout.

articles.title: Point a tool at a folder and ask about the files
articles.question: I want to point something at a folder and then ask questions about what's in it. What should I use?
articles.summary: Index the folder with one command, read the map of what XERJ found, then let an agent query it over MCP instead of opening the files one by one.

articles.title: RAG without a vector database
articles.question: How do I build RAG without a vector database?
articles.summary: Build a RAG retrieval layer on one XERJ index. One hybrid request fuses BM25 and kNN with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and no second service runs.

articles.title: What is Reciprocal Rank Fusion?
articles.question: What is reciprocal rank fusion and when should I use it?
articles.summary: Reciprocal Rank Fusion scores a document by 1 divided by k plus its rank in each list. XERJ uses k 60, and this page checks the arithmetic by hand.

articles.title: How does XERJ combine BM25 and kNN?
articles.question: How does XERJ combine BM25 and kNN?
articles.summary: One hybrid request carries a BM25 sub-query and a kNN sub-query against one index, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges their ranked lists into a single result list.

articles.title: How do I check my code index actually finished?
articles.question: My codebase indexer says indexed but I don't see my code. How do I check it actually finished?
articles.summary: Compare 4 numbers: files on disk, the dry-run plan, autoindex status, and the index count. A captured run cut 64 files to a 3-file plan, naming a rule per gap.

articles.title: How do I estimate folder-indexing time?
articles.question: How long will it take to index a folder for search?
articles.summary: XERJ measures a client-side extraction floor during a dry run and can stop at a decision gate with exit 4. On 2,500 PDFs the floor was 2.2 min, the run 157.7 s.

articles.title: Why does a folder search miss files on disk?
articles.question: Why would a folder search miss files that I can see on disk?
articles.summary: XERJ prints one line per ignore rule and stores a refusal reason per file. A capture reconciles 26 files on disk to 1 indexed, 2 refused and 23 excluded.

articles.title: What do the xerj autoindex exit codes mean?
articles.question: What does indexer exit code 3 mean?
articles.summary: xerj autoindex exits 0 complete, 3 completed-with-junk, 4 needs-a-decision, 2 usage and 1 on an endpoint or journal failure. Only 4 is asking you a question.

articles.title: Is there a single-binary local search engine?
articles.question: Is there a single-binary local search engine I can just run?
articles.summary: XERJ runs from one native binary with no container and no JVM. A measured capture records 3 linked libraries and a 1.071 s cold start to the first HTTP 200.

articles.title: What can I use for low-volume log search?
articles.question: Free or cheap alternative for low volume log management and searching?
articles.summary: XERJ indexes plain-text logs on one node with exact error counts and sub-millisecond filters. A measured ladder stops at 16 MB: memory grows about 200x the corpus.

articles.title: How do I read autoindex progress?
articles.question: How can I see whether folder indexing is still working?
articles.summary: XERJ prints xerj-bar, xerj-progress and a final xerj-done line. On a single large file the percentage stays at 0.0%, so read since_progress_s and waiting_on.

articles.title: The indexer died overnight. Do I start over?
articles.question: The indexer died overnight. Do I have to start over?
articles.summary: XERJ keeps a resume journal in the state directory, so re-running autoindex is idempotent. A capture reached 82,231 documents and matched a clean control run.

articles.title: Why is reindexing my files taking forever?
articles.question: Reindexing my files is taking forever. What usually causes that?
articles.summary: A measured XERJ _reindex moved 100,000 documents in 20,836 ms on one node. Read the batches, created and failures fields to tell slow progress from no progress.

articles.title: What is XERJ?
articles.question: What is XERJ?
articles.summary: XERJ is an Apache-2.0 single Rust binary that indexes a local folder with one command and answers search, agent memory and MCP calls from the same process.

articles.title: Improve a basic FAISS RAG pipeline
articles.question: How can I improve a basic FAISS RAG pipeline?
articles.summary: Move the chunk store into one XERJ index and fuse BM25 with kNN. Two request shapes that a FAISS user reaches for first both return HTTP 400.

articles.title: When does XERJ kNN use an exact scan instead of HNSW?
articles.question: Why is filtered kNN slower than unfiltered?
articles.summary: A filter takes kNN off the HNSW graph and onto an exact scan whose cost scales with vectors scanned. This page explains when that happens and publishes no timing.

articles.title: Vector database or full-text search for a folder?
articles.question: What's the actual difference between a vector database and full-text search?
articles.summary: Full-text search matches tokens, kNN matches vectors, hybrid fuses both. XERJ serves all three from one index over an indexed folder, so the choice is a clause.
